Mira Patel: Bringing up comet-11b (int4) on canary cluster. Seeing OOMs when batch_size >= 8 during decoding. Logs show sudden KV allocations spike then OOM. Anyone seen this pattern?

Sanjeev Rao: Can you paste the tail of the runtime log around the OOM? Also which defaults are you using (max_new_tokens / prefetch / kv_eviction)?

Mira Patel: Here’s the relevant snippet from the canary node (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-19T22:11:02Z] decode: allocate_kv: requested 120MB -> commit ok
[2026-03-19T22:11:02Z] decode: allocate_kv: requested 480MB -> commit ok
[2026-03-19T22:11:03Z] decode: allocate_kv: requested 1024MB -> failed: OOM
runtime: OOM while allocating KV cache, total_used=13.2GB, host_free=300MB
```
Defaults: max_new_tokens=1024, prefetch=true, max_batch_size=16, kv_eviction_threshold=0.8

Hanna Li: two quick levers: 1) lower max_new_tokens default (1024 is high for most conv workloads) 2) drop max_batch_size to 4 while we investigate. That usually avoids hitting fragmentation/peak alloc. Try: `rctl update model-config --model comet-11b --set max_new_tokens=256 --set max_batch_size=4` and disable prefetch on canary.

Alex Gomez: FWIW that allocation pattern looks like fragmentation + big contiguous KV allocation failing. We've seen glibc malloc fragment on long-running JVM/C++ processes. Quick experiments: use jemalloc or tcmalloc on the worker process: `export LD_PRELOAD=/opt/jemalloc/lib/libjemalloc.so && systemctl restart redwood-runtime` Also consider enabling KV trim-on-alloc: `kv_trim_on_alloc=true` or set `kv_eviction_threshold=0.65`.

Mira Patel: Applied max_new_tokens=256 and max_batch_size=4, prefetch=false on the canary pool. Re-run of the failure workload (same QPS) for ~30m: no OOMs so far, but p50 latency increased ~12%. Is that acceptable for the canary? :eyes:

Sanjeev Rao: 12% p50 bump is acceptable for a short mitigation window. Longer term we want throughput back. Next steps: 1) try jemalloc to reduce fragmentation; 2) experiment with adaptive prefetch window smaller (e.g., prefetch_window=32) so we get some batching without the big KV peaks. You can run a bench like: `rctl bench --model comet-11b --load tests/comet_canary_prompts.json --qps 50 --duration 600` to compare.

Hanna Li: Also must run the quantization quality regressions — int4 can change tokenization edge cases. Run the nightly eval suite and diff scores before/after: `rd-eval run --suite comet-evals/conv-quality-v1 --model comet-11b-int4 --baseline comet-11b-fp16` and post delta. If regressions > 1.5% on top-1 we may need per-layer remapping or mixed-precision fallback.

Mira Patel: Got it. I'll run the bench + eval tonight and roll jemalloc on one canary host first. Will post logs and eval diffs here. cc @eng-oncall-bot :thumbsup:

eng-oncall-bot: Noted. Creating incident stub: INC-2026-0319-COMET-ONBOARD. Assigning to Mira Patel and oncall.

Alex Gomez: If jemalloc reduces fragmentation but we still need throughput, consider a two-tier rollout: keep max_new_tokens=256 for default user route, but add a high-throughput route with pinned instances and KV prewarm for trusted enterprise traffic. That gives us predictable capacity without exposing everyone to OOM risk.

Mira Patel: Sounds like a plan. I'll document the steps in the canary runbook and follow up with results tomorrow morning. Thanks all :thumbsup:
